findings.pdf_says: BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED        0                    £  n  <  256 [2**8]   /  BINARY-SHORT UNSIGNED  0  £ n < 65536 [2**16]  /  BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED  0  £ n < 4294967296 [2**32]  /  BINARY-DOUBLE UNSIGNED  0  £ n < 2**64   (the '£' is the glyph the ISO PDF itself paints: a Symbol-font 'less-than-or-equal' at code point 0xA3 emitted under a text-font encoding, so it images as a pound sign)
findings.markdown_says:
| BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED | 0 | £ n < | 256 [2\*\*8] |
| BINARY-SHORT UNSIGNED | 0 | £ n < | 65536 [2\*\*16] |
| BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED | 0 | £ n < | 4294967296 [2\*\*32] |
| BINARY-DOUBLE UNSIGNED | 0 | £ n < | 2\*\*64 |
findings.why_it_matters: NOT a transcription slip - the markdown faithfully copies the broken glyph the PDF prints, so a verifier re-reading page 537 will see '£' in both. The defect is inherited from ISO's own PDF font encoding, and it destroys normative content: 13.18.60.4 General rule 12 defines the minimum range each binary-N usage must represent, and the operator in the left-hand comparison is what says whether the lower bound is inclusive. Read literally, '0 £ n < 256' has no meaning; the intended relation for every UNSIGNED row is '0 <= n < 2**8' etc. (the SIGNED rows correctly show '<' because -128 is excluded, and an unsigned item must be able to hold 0, so the unsigned operator can only be '<='). Because the same mis-mapped 0xA3 will recur wherever the standard prints a 'less-than-or-equal', this is a pattern to sweep, not a one-off.
findings.suggested_repair: Transcribe the four UNSIGNED rows with the mathematically intended operator, '≤ n <' (or '<= n <'), and add a one-line editorial note at the table - e.g. 'NOTE (transcription) The published PDF images this operator as £; it is a Symbol-font ≤ (0xA3) emitted under a text-font encoding.' Then grep specs/ISO_COBOL.md for every remaining bare '£' and apply the same correction with the same note.

findings.pdf_says: Sub-items are printed indented under their parents: the continuation paragraph 'If a report footing is defined and is not on a page by itself, the page footing on the last page is immediately followed by the report footing.' sits at the body indent of General rule 6) f) (it is the tail of f)); 'g) The report footing, if defined, is printed, ...' sits at the a)-g) marker indent under 6); '7) The upper limit is defined to be the uppermost permitted line ...' sits at the top-level rule indent; 'a) The upper limit for a report heading or a page heading ...' through 'g) The upper limit for a report footing that does not appear on a page by itself ...' are indented one level under 7); and '1. If the body group is a control heading at the same or a higher control level ...' through '4. If the body group is a control footing, ...' are indented a further level under 7) d).
findings.markdown_says:
Every one of those lines is flush left at column 0 with no indentation, e.g.:
"If a report footing is defined and is not on a page by itself, the page footing on the last page is immediately followed by the report footing."
"g) The report footing, if defined, is printed, as the very last report group in the report, ..."
"7) The upper limit is defined to be the uppermost permitted line on the page that may be occupied by the report group's first line. It is calculated as follows:"
"a) The upper limit for a report heading or a page heading where no report heading appears on the same page is the line given by the HEADING integer."
"1. If the body group is a control heading at the same or a higher control level than the highest-level control heading that has an OR PAGE phrase, the upper limit is the line given by the FIRST DETAIL integer."
"g) The upper limit for a report footing that does not appear on a page by itself is the line following the last line of the page footing, ..."
findings.why_it_matters: Indentation is the only thing that binds a sub-item to its parent rule in 13.18.57.4, and here it is the only thing lost. Flattened, page 528 shows two different 'g)' items at the same level as '7)' - one belonging to General rule 6) (carried over from page 527) and one belonging to 7) - so a reader or a tool walking the list cannot tell which rule either 'g)' qualifies, and the '1.' through '4.' cases read as top-level enumerations instead of the four sub-cases of 7) d) (upper limit for a body group when some control heading carries OR PAGE). The transcription preserves this nesting correctly on pages 527, 529 and 535 of the same clause, which confirms page 528 is drift rather than a house style.
findings.suggested_repair: Re-indent the page-528 slice to match the convention already used on pages 527/529/535: three spaces before 'a)'..'g)' of rule 7) and before the 'g)' that belongs to rule 6), six spaces before '1.'..'4.' under 7) d), and three spaces before the 'If a report footing is defined ...' continuation paragraph so it stays attached to 6) f).
